item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports combining local sequence modeling with global item transitions. [TGCL4SR (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) combines a temporal item-transition graph with a Transformer sequence encoder, using graph contrastive learning and time intervals. [Semantic and temporal-aware hybrid embedding (2026)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10462-025-11483-5) is particularly close to the proposed architecture: Markov transition probabilities, content cosine similarity, personalized PageRank normalization, temporal decay, and GCN smoothing produce embeddings for SASRec. Its metadata includes titles and categories; the present benchmark permits titles/descriptions but excludes item categories, so direct replication needs adaptation.\n\nCold-start research also highlights a tension between preserving content information and adapting embeddings to collaborative signals. [Let It Go? Not Quite (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19473) proposes frozen content embeddings plus a small trainable residual, reporting improvements across text and audio settings. These results do not establish equivalent gains from text features learned from scratch. A practical hypothesis within the stated constraints: retain SASRec, add sparse transition scores built exclusively from training histories, and encode titles/descriptions through TF-IDF projection or pooled randomly initialized token embeddings. Blend the three signals with validation-tuned weights, potentially conditioned on history length or item frequency. This is an implementation proposal inferred from the literature, not a verified benchmark result; test sequence-only, transition-only, text-only, and combined variants using the same macro validation HR@10."}
